title: Parse success is not a lossless JSON or URL query serialization round trip
applies_when: A trace or protocol exporter interpolates text or dynamic keys into JSON, or a URL builder hand-escapes a query value. Suspect content corruption as well as syntax errors; inspect the exact downstream decoding context.
lesson: Validate both syntax and exact decoded content. A backslash sequence such as a literal Windows path can form valid JSON but decode into tabs/newlines; deleting quotes can silently rename markers. Use the format's encoder on each textual value/key and remove the surrounding hand-written quotes, rather than sanitizing or double-encoding. Exercise the actual database/file exporter and decompress/parse its output. Include ordinary and Unicode controls plus quotes, backslashes and control characters; assert names/descriptions are identical to the input, not merely that json.load succeeds. For a URL query value, test +, &, #, % and already-escaped-looking input: parse the constructed URL, require the exact decoded value, unchanged adjacent parameters and no accidental fragment. Manual replacement of only spaces, slashes and question marks can pass ordinary examples while changing C++ or truncating a file name at #. Check numeric fields and event envelopes separately so a text repair does not change their types. Follow producer types: a graph kernel count is numeric, not evidence that arbitrary text reaches that field. Search the original upstream implementation when working with a vendored converter before inventing a separate escaping routine.
avoid_when: Do not impose lossless text where the protocol explicitly requires normalization/redaction. A query value, path segment and complete URL need different encoding; QueryUnescape treats + as space while PathUnescape does not. Preserve any explicit canonical signing/normalization contract instead of assuming byte-identical encodings. Match the installed producer's source revision, including native submodules, against current upstream before proposing a new repair: an old wheel can reproduce an already-addressed defect. A SQLite fixture proves conversion of supported rows, not live device capture, current producer-schema compatibility or end-to-end performance. Direct component loading can isolate a stdlib exporter from an unavailable server package, but must be reported separately from installed-package/registered CI execution. A Go util-package round trip does not execute the whole backend, live ClawHub requests, Windows or the minimum-Go matrix. These known cases are not a prospective selector comparison or a paper result.

evidence.note: EncodeQuery replaces only space, / and ?. Source mechanism, not proof of whole-backend or live-service behavior. EncodePath is a separate context and is not changed by the query repair.
Search, FetchFile and Download insert EncodeQuery output into q, path and slug values. These are pinned source callers, not executed ClawHub integration.
Go's standard library provides QueryEscape/QueryUnescape for query values and a distinct PathEscape/PathUnescape contract; URL parsing success alone does not assert original content.

Owner-known repair, not a new Scout discovery or upstream PR: the same 39 value/parameter combinations have 18 old-production failures and 21 passing controls; repaired production passes all. Linux Go1.27.2 actual util ordinary/race suites each pass 100 test/subtest events with no skips; vet/gofmt pass. The 43 focused events include four parents, not 43 independent bugs. Test parsing is not live backend execution or full dependency-graph verification; no performance, acceptance or selector-efficiency claim.

Pinned SGLang converter interpolates operation text directly and removes quotes from API/marker/frame text. Counter and graph fields have different producer types; not every formatting placeholder establishes a user-controlled text defect.

Independent real-SQLite to gzip/JSON comparison: baseline has 8 JSON decoding errors, 2 silent corruption failures and 4 passing controls; repaired component passes all 14 subcases in 3 test methods on native Windows CPython 3.12/3.14. Registered package execution is blocked by resource import on Windows; no AMD capture/performance/merge claim.
The converter's original upstream already uses json.dumps for marker/API/operation text, supporting reuse of a standard encoder rather than a novel escaping algorithm or a whole upstream sync.
Kineto revision pinned by PyTorch commit70d99e9 (Torch2.11.0) sanitizes op_name without escaping quotes. This identifies the old producer mechanism, not current upstream behavior.

Current pinned source calls escapeQuotesForJSON after sanitizing event names. It still replaces backslashes with slashes; quote validity and lossless text are separate properties. Source-only comparison, not execution of a current wheel or proof of all trace fields.
